analyst_view.overall: Early view: Athletic open the post-break round on Friday night with no fit centre-forward: Gorka Guruzeta is out for the season with a cruciate tear, Asier Hierro has a knee ligament injury and Maroan Sannadi is still recovering, so the Williams brothers carry the attack. Espanyol play only their second league game under Eder Sarabia, who replaced the sacked Manolo González and started with a 0-0 draw against Deportivo in which his side kept 64% of the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Athletic have no recognised No. 9 (Guruzeta, Hierro and Sannadi all injured), and Espanyol are without striker Kike García, who one injury list has out until December. Sarabia's first game ended 0-0 with keeper Ángel Fortuño unbeaten.

corners.text: The site expects 10.0 corners, 6.5 of them for Athletic. Sarabia wants Espanyol to keep the ball (they had 64% against Deportivo), which should cut into Athletic's territory, and without a target man Terzić's side cross less. Athletic took only four corners at El Sadar last time out.

cards.text: The model has 5.0 cards and I see no reason to move it yet. Espanyol picked up four yellows against Deportivo, mostly for dangerous play, while Athletic had just one at Osasuna; the referee, who will decide a lot here, is not yet known.

shots.text: The site expects 26.1 shots, 17.7 from Athletic. Athletic managed 16 at Osasuna, and with no striker more of their efforts will come from Sancet and Navarro outside the box rather than in volume. A Sarabia side that holds possession should also limit the number of Athletic attacks.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Losing Guruzeta and Hierro removes Athletic's main finishers in the box, and Espanyol landed few efforts on target against Deportivo. A total of 7 or 8 looks more likely than 9 or more.
